semis.why: Lean goes AGAINST the -1.1% thin pre-market gap (14/18 red, ASML -1.6, SKHY ADR -2.7, no volume): the same ~-0.9% pre-market dip on 09-21 and 09-22 was bought into large up closes (SOX 6 straight up days, memory-led Tue per Bloomberg); Asia chip proxies closed GREEN today (Samsung +3.2, Hynix +1.0, TSMC TW +1.2) so the regional buyer did not flinch; Meta Connect (the Muse story that started the CPU leg) lands in-session; oil ~$90 from ~$102 on 09-16 removes the macro headwind. Against: stretched (+11.1% median vs 50d, SOXX 5d +12.45%, AMD rsi73 / INTC rsi71) and the Xi meeting Thursday. Firm = close above the pre-market ref, not above Tuesday's close.

big_tech.why: All 5 green pre-market (median +0.29%, MSFT +0.9); QQQ -0.19% is its chip weight, which should fade if the chip dip is bought; META Connect keynote is the in-session catalyst. dont_add: META rsi78 / +21% vs 50d on 2.33x volume, QQQ 5d +4.55%.

market.why: ES +0.01% / NQ -0.07%, VIX 14.2 in contango; the non-tech side has no catalyst tonight and the Trump-Xi meeting is Thursday, so a mild tech-led gain is diluted inside the band.

sg_banks.why: Target = Thu SGX close (05:00 ET Thu), before any summit outcome; STI -0.14% today with only OCBC (-1.1%) moving; tonight's US session is the only input and the lean there is mild.

summary.bottom_line: Hold chips and big tech, but don't add at these levels. This morning's dip in chips looks like the same dip that got bought on Monday and Tuesday, and I expect it to be bought again tonight.
summary.where_we_are: 19:27 SGT Wednesday = 07:27 ET. US pre-market; the US opens at 21:30 SGT. Singapore is closed for the day. No US data tonight. Meta's Connect keynote falls during the US session. China's leader Xi arrives in Washington on Wednesday evening US time, and he meets Trump at the White House on Thursday (Sep 24).
summary.macro_attribution: Oil is the macro input that matters. US crude fell from about $102 on Sep 16 (catalysts.json rate map) to about $90 now (tape) on US–Iran talks, and it bounced 0.7% this morning. The 10-year yield (4.97%), the dollar (+0.3%) and the fear gauge, VIX (14), barely moved. Gold's -1.1% is the biggest move in percentage terms but it isn't driving anything. My lean assumes oil stays down: a sharp rebound would remove half of what has powered this rally.
what_happened: Chips rose for a sixth straight day on Tuesday. Memory led: Sandisk +7%, Micron +5% (Bloomberg, Sep 22). That came after Monday's AMD +10% / Intel +12% surge on Meta's Muse shopping agent (Bloomberg, Sep 21). The chip ETF is up 12.5% in five days and sits 11% above its 50-day average (tape). That makes this a stretched run, not a rebound.

Before the open the chip ETF is down 1.1%, with 15 of 18 names red. The weakest are equipment (ASML, which makes chip-printing machines, -1.6%) and SK Hynix's US listing (-2.7%) (tape). Pre-market trades carry no volume, so treat this dip as thin. Similar pre-market dips on Monday and Tuesday both turned into big up closes.
Asia bought chips today rather than selling them: Samsung +3.2% and SK Hynix +1.0% in Seoul, TSMC +1.2% in Taipei. Hong Kong fell 1.0% ahead of the summit (tape).

Big tech is quietly green, with all five names up before the open and Microsoft leading at +0.9% (tape). Meta heads into its own event at RSI 78 (overbought on that momentum gauge), 21% above its 50-day average (tape).
Futures are flat: S&P +0.0%, Nasdaq -0.1% (tape; CNBC, Sep 23). VIX is at 14, with calm readings further out (tape).

per_group.semis: Slightly up from here, meaning a close above this morning's pre-market price. Buyers have stepped in at the open two days running, Asian memory and TSMC closed green, and Meta's event lands mid-session. Memory makers (Micron, Sandisk) and chip designers (AMD, Nvidia) should lead the recovery, with equipment (ASML) staying the weak spot.
per_group.big_tech: Slightly up. All five are green before the open with Microsoft leading, and Meta's keynote is the day's catalyst. The index is only red because of its chip holdings, and that drag should fade if chips recover.
per_group.market: Flat. Gains in tech get diluted by the rest of the index, which has no reason to move the night before the Trump–Xi meeting.
per_group.sg_banks: Flat at Thursday's close. Tonight's US session is the only new input before the Xi meeting, and OCBC's -1.1% was the only real move today.

change_my_mind: Chips still below the pre-market level an hour after the open (22:30 SGT): nobody is buying the dip, and chips flip to down.
Meta falls after its keynote: investors are selling the story that started this rally, and chips and big tech both flip to down.
Oil back above about $94, or the 10-year yield through 5.00%: the macro tailwind is reversing, and the whole market flips to down.
A chip-export or tariff headline tied to the summit before the close: chips flip to down.
summary.confidence: the dip-buying pattern is only two days old, chips are stretched after six up days, and the Trump–Xi meeting is one day away.
summary.cant_know: Whether today is the day a six-day run ends. Nothing on the tape can tell a pause from a top.
summary.the_call: Up from here, but only modestly. Chips open weak, get bought, and close above this morning's pre-market price, a moderate move (roughly half a percent to one and a half) and the biggest of any group. Big tech edges up with Meta's event, a mild move. The broad market and Singapore banks barely move.
